note: Territory index. To add a nation: add its data file under public/data/web/territories/ and one entry here. No code change needed. Colors: Okabe-Ito colorblind-safe palette, one per nation.

nations.name: Chickasaw
nations.note: Extent shown is the 1786 Treaty of Hopewell frame; its southern edge is not fixed by the sources.
nations.mapNote: General area (1786 Hopewell frame): approximate, not a boundary.

nations.name: Cherokee
nations.mapNote: General area: Kentucky part of the 1771 cession and Chickamauga counties. Approximate, low-medium confidence, not a boundary. Treaty lines dashed outside Kentucky.
nations.note: Main-map shape = sourced treaty/survey lines (1768, 1770, 1771) plus the Chickamauga county footprint. Pre-1768 Kentucky use has no dated boundary and is not drawn.

nations.name: Shawnee
nations.mapNote: General area claimed or used, c.1715–1795: effectively most of present Kentucky (drawn as the whole state, the most generous estimate) plus Ohio town counties. Approximate, low-medium confidence, not a boundary. 1774 Ohio River line on top.
nations.note: Main-map shape = general area claimed or used (Kentucky outline, most generous estimate of “most of Kentucky”), the 1774 Ohio River line and the Ohio town counties. No boundary is sourced.

nations.name: Six Nations (Haudenosaunee)
nations.mapNote: General area associated with the Six Nations (hatched): Kentucky east of the Tennessee River, clipped to Kentucky. A claim by treaty cession, not where people lived; approximate, low-medium confidence, not a boundary. Ohio River solid in Kentucky, dashed beyond.
nations.note: Kentucky east of the Tennessee River was sold to the Crown at Fort Stanwix 1768 on a Six Nations conquest claim that the Cherokee and Shawnee disputed. Outside Kentucky only the dashed Ohio River is drawn.

nations.name: Mingo
nations.mapNote: Presence, no mapped boundary. Three approximate points (Mingo Town OH 1770, Yellow Creek 1774, McClelland’s Station raid 1776). Kentucky camp sites unknown, not drawn.
nations.note: Presence only: sourced towns and raid sites; no Kentucky camp areas are known or drawn.
